evaluation.positioning_hook: A brilliant Nairobi hacker is forced into a cyber-heist that exposes his parents’ criminal empire, then turns the city’s most dangerous men against each other to find his missing sister.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The hook is easy to grasp and the cybercrime-plus-family-betrayal engine gives it a clear thriller audience. It reads more niche than four-quadrant because the dialogue-heavy, tech-forward approach and local specificity narrow the immediate commercial lane.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The premise lands early: Mark is a gifted hacker, his parents are arrested, and a mysterious fixer pushes him into a bank job tied to his sister and a hidden criminal network. The story engine is clear, though the layers of Regency, Stylet Directory, Berk, Jackie, and Tony take a beat to fully sort.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: Mark has a strong contradiction on the page — gifted, arrogant, isolated, and still emotionally tethered to family — and Tony gives him a useful counterweight. The supporting cast is functional and memorable in moments, but the emotional center is still carried mostly by Mark’s attitude and the family reveal.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: A Nairobi-set cybercrime thriller with a mother who is more technically gifted than her son and a family crime syndicate built around hacking gives the script a distinct angle. The execution leans into familiar thriller beats and broad villainy, so the freshness comes more from setting and premise than from formal daring.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: The script keeps moving through arrests, dates, bank intrusion, torture, and a final reveal-heavy showdown, so there is always another turn. The momentum is sometimes driven by explanation and reversals rather than clean escalation, which keeps it engaging but not yet fully propulsive.

resonant_originality.reasoning: The idea of a young hacker discovering his parents founded a criminal network and that his missing sister is tied to the same machine feels fresh and immediately legible. The combination of cybercrime, family betrayal, and Nairobi institutional texture gives the premise a memorable identity.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: The script builds a specific ecosystem of homes, law offices, banks, police units, and criminal infrastructure in Nairobi, with cybercrime laws and local power structures shaping the plot. The world is story-generating and feels larger than the immediate scenes, even when the dialogue occasionally explains the system more than dramatizes it.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The tone is unmistakably heightened: comic insults, family melodrama, cyber jargon, and sudden brutality all live in the same space. That blend gives the script personality, though the shifts between banter, procedural explanation, and extreme violence are broad enough that the tonal identity is still settling.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: Beneath the heist mechanics, the script is really about inheritance, loyalty, and a family built on secrecy, which gives it more emotional reserve than a standard cyber-thriller. The Jackie reveal, the parents’ criminal history, and Tony’s double life all suggest a deeper backstory that could keep paying off.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: Mark and Tony carry the central dynamic well, and the parents, Sophie, Jackie, Bernard, and Monica all add pressure in different directions. The ensemble has useful friction, but most relationships still orbit Mark rather than generating fully independent story energy.

casting_characteristics: Kenyan/Nairobi setting with locally grounded adult casting
One principal female hacker/mother role with strong technical authority
One principal older antagonist role with physical cane use and violent outbursts

locations.interior_exterior_ratio: Mostly interior with several exterior city and action sequences

technical.vfx_details: Primarily screen inserts, interface graphics, surveillance feeds, and digital readouts; no heavy creature or environment work.
technical.sfx_needs: Gunfire, blood effects, car explosion, practical violence, breakaway glass, and crowd-control action beats.

rights_flags.detail: The script references The Pentagon and the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act No. 5 of 2018 as plot context.

platform_fit.recommended_lane: Streaming or premium-cable crime thriller lane with international-local flavor
platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model; best positioned as festival-to-platform or streamer original with thriller marketing around cybercrime, family betrayal, and a contained action footprint.

cost.note: Contemporary locations keep the footprint manageable, but the bank breach, SWAT raid, gun battle, and car explosion push it above a microbudget lane.

cast.note: The story depends on a handful of strong adult roles — Mark, Tony, Jackie, Bernard, the parents, Sophie, Monica, and the bank team — but not on star-heavy ensemble scale.

location.note: The script moves through homes, offices, a bank, a cafe, a restaurant, a police station, a courtroom, a warehouse, a prison, and a cemetery, with several night exteriors.

content.note: The story includes torture, execution-style violence, gun battles, blood, threats, and sexual assault testimony, which narrows platform and rating flexibility.

rights.note: Several brand names and a named legal statute appear on the page, but the script is not built around major third-party IP or life-rights dependencies.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Nairobi gives the thriller a real edge.
strengths.what_it_means: The setting is not decorative; it gives the script a specific institutional and social texture that can separate it from generic cyber-thrillers. Buyers looking for exportable local stories with a global genre spine will see a marketable identity here.
strengths.evidence: The story moves through Nairobi homes, courts, police action, and the Seraphic Bank ecosystem, with local legal and cybercrime references woven into the plot.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Mark is built as a contradiction.
strengths.what_it_means: He is smart enough to drive the plot, prickly enough to create friction, and emotionally incomplete enough to sustain a feature arc. That gives an actor a role with swagger, vulnerability, and moral ambiguity in one package.
strengths.evidence: He can out-hack a bank, talks down to everyone, and still cracks when the story turns to his parents, Tony, and Jackie.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The family reveal is the engine.
strengths.what_it_means: The script’s biggest commercial lever is that the hero’s personal mystery is also the criminal conspiracy, which ties the emotional and thriller tracks together. That kind of reveal structure is attractive to buyers because it promises both plot momentum and franchiseable backstory.
strengths.evidence: Mark learns his parents founded The Regency and that Jackie is tied to the larger power structure just as the bank job and the Stylet Directory collide.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The mother role has real showcase value.
strengths.what_it_means: Rose is not just support; she is the kind of technically brilliant, morally compromised parent role that can anchor a prestige performance and give the movie a memorable female center. That is the sort of part that attracts seasoned dramatic actors who want intelligence, authority, and secrecy in the same role.
strengths.evidence: She helps Mark with the hacking, outperforms him at the keyboard, and still insists the work is criminal and shameful.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The villain is theatrical and legible.
strengths.what_it_means: Bernard’s cane, volatility, and ritualized violence make him easy to market as a memorable antagonist rather than a faceless corporate bad guy. Character actors who like big, operatic turns will see a role with physicality, menace, and scene-stealing monologues.
strengths.evidence: His Double Roulette story, the Monica execution, and the warehouse beating of Fred all establish a vivid villain signature.

strengths.what_it_means: The hacking sequences are built around screens, live feeds, and countdown pressure, which keeps the action producible while still feeling kinetic. That makes the script easier to mount than a VFX-heavy thriller and more attractive to buyers who want contained spectacle.
strengths.evidence: The Juicebox operation, the bank IT intercuts, and the keylogger/USB setup all translate cyber action into filmable beats.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Tony gives the movie a human counterweight.
strengths.what_it_means: He functions as the audience’s bridge into Mark’s world and gives the story a friendship dynamic that can carry humor, betrayal, and emotional payoff. That makes the project more castable because it offers a second strong male role with warmth and tension, not just a lone protagonist.
strengths.evidence: Tony coaches Mark through the date, helps with the bank fallout, and is later revealed to be working a deeper angle with Jackie.

whats_special.headline: DOUBLE ROULETTE has a clean commercial spine: a gifted Nairobi hacker gets pulled into a bank heist that turns into a family conspiracy, a missing-sister hunt, and a war with the city’s criminal elite. The script’s best selling points are its specific setting, its vivid villain, and a lead role built on arrogance, intelligence, and emotional damage — exactly the kind of part that can launch a breakout performance.

lead_characters.name: MARK MASILA
lead_characters.hook: Mark is a brilliant, socially abrasive young hacker who treats the digital world like home and human connection like an inconvenience. He has the kind of cocky intelligence that makes him magnetic and insufferable at the same time, but the script keeps revealing the hurt underneath — a son desperate for approval, a brother haunted by Jackie, and a young man whose genius keeps dragging him into moral territory he barely understands.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Rami Malek in Mr. Robot — a hyper-specific, internally charged tech savant whose intelligence is inseparable from alienation. It gives an actor the chance to play precision, ego, panic, and emotional collapse in the same role, with a feature-length arc that can pivot from smug control to raw vulnerability.

lead_characters.name: MRS. MASILA ROSE
lead_characters.hook: Rose is the warmest person in the room and, quietly, one of the most dangerous minds in the story. She can move from affectionate mother to technical co-conspirator to moral conscience without losing her charm, which makes her feel like the family’s hidden operating system.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Viola Davis in Fences — a parent whose love, intelligence, and authority all live in the same frame. It gives a seasoned actress a role with command, wit, and the chance to reveal how much of the family’s machinery she actually understands.

lead_characters.name: MR. MASILA JOHN
lead_characters.hook: John is a strict patriarch who believes order, discipline, and the law are the only things holding chaos back. He is intimidating, proud, and emotionally blunt, but the script lets him carry real pain around Jackie, Mark, and the family’s buried history.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Bryan Cranston in Breaking Bad’s early domestic scenes — a father whose authority is built on control, but whose private life is full of contradiction. It gives an actor a role that can play sternness, wounded pride, and buried guilt without ever leaving the family table.

lead_characters.name: TONY BARAKA
lead_characters.hook: Tony is Mark’s polished, socially fluent friend and fixer, the guy who can move between law, crime, and friendship without ever looking fully at home in any of them. He reads as the easygoing best friend until the script starts revealing how much he knows, how much he’s hiding, and how deeply he’s tied into the larger game.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Mahershala Ali in Moonlight’s adult sections — a calm, controlled presence whose restraint carries hidden stakes. It gives an actor the chance to play charm as camouflage and to land the emotional gut-punch of a friend who may be helping and betraying at the same time.

lead_characters.name: SOPHIE
lead_characters.hook: Sophie is bright, fast, and socially fearless, the kind of young woman who can read a room and puncture Mark’s ego in one sentence. She has a playful intelligence that makes her feel like a real counterpoint to him, and her bluntness gives the movie one of its cleanest human voices.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Ayo Edebiri in The Bear — quick, observant, and capable of turning sharp dialogue into character revelation. It gives a young actress a role that can play wit, intelligence, and emotional clarity without becoming a generic love interest.

lead_characters.name: JACKIE
lead_characters.hook: Jackie is the missing sister who returns as a power player, not a victim, and that reversal gives the story its final charge. She is stylish, hard-edged, emotionally guarded, and clearly shaped by years inside the machine Mark has only just discovered.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Jodie Comer in Killing Eve — a woman whose charm and menace can coexist in the same beat. It gives an actress a late-story power reveal with emotional history, authority, and the ability to turn family intimacy into a threat.

lead_characters.name: BERNARD MASAWE / MR. BERK
lead_characters.hook: Bernard is a limping, cane-wielding power broker who treats cruelty like a business tool and performance art. He is theatrical, sadistic, and oddly self-mythologizing, which makes him feel larger than the room and more dangerous because of it.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Javier Bardem in No Country for Old Men — a villain whose calm, ritualized menace makes every scene feel like a trap. It gives an actor a role with monologue space, physical presence, and the kind of memorable cruelty that can define a movie.

lead_characters.name: JAVAN MUTISO
lead_characters.hook: Javan is the polished intermediary who speaks in controlled, transactional language and never quite reveals where his loyalty ends. He functions as the story’s human interface to the larger conspiracy, which makes him feel slippery and useful in equal measure.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Michael Shannon in supporting-thriller mode — a man who can make a messenger feel like a threat. It gives a character actor a role built on contained intensity, ambiguity, and the pleasure of withholding.

lead_characters.name: MONICA
lead_characters.hook: Monica is the secretary who initially reads as cautious and procedural, then becomes the story’s most painful human witness. She carries fear, shame, and moral courage in a small number of scenes, which makes her presence land hard.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Patricia Clarkson in a compact drama role — a woman whose quiet scene work can carry enormous emotional weight. It gives an actress a contained but memorable part with trauma, conscience, and a devastating payoff.

lead_characters.name: GORDY
lead_characters.hook: Gordy is the eager junior hacker who wants to belong to Mark’s world and prove he can keep up. He brings youthful energy and comic friction to the Juicebox operation, but he also helps show how dangerous Mark’s orbit is for anyone who steps into it.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Lucas Hedges in a supporting indie role — a nervous, eager younger collaborator whose enthusiasm makes the stakes feel real. It gives a young actor a chance to play speed, insecurity, and loyalty under pressure.

lead_characters.name: FRED BAHATI
lead_characters.hook: Fred is the bank’s swaggering ICT director, all ego and control until the system starts slipping away from him. He is a useful institutional antagonist because he makes the bank feel like a living organism with its own hierarchy and panic response.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Shea Whigham in a pressure-cooker supporting role — a man whose authority starts to crack the second the room turns against him. It gives an actor a sharp, scene-driving part with panic, bluster, and institutional humiliation.

lead_characters.name: DANIEL
lead_characters.hook: Daniel is the tired, older bank engineer who knows enough to be useful and too much to be comfortable. He gives the bank side of the story a human face and a sense of age, fatigue, and professional resignation.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of David Strathairn in a procedural thriller — a weary professional whose competence is undercut by the machine around him. It gives a character actor a grounded role that can play intelligence, embarrassment, and institutional pressure.

director_appeal.hook: A director who wants to make a propulsive crime thriller with local specificity and a big emotional reveal.
director_appeal.fit_profile: Established indie or genre directors with at least one or two features, especially those who like performance-forward thrillers, family betrayal, and clean visual storytelling over heavy spectacle. This material rewards someone who can stage cyber action, keep the family drama legible, and make the final reveal feel inevitable rather than merely surprising.
director_appeal.detail: The movie gives a director a chance to balance contained interiors, procedural tension, and sudden violence without needing a giant effects canvas. It will attract filmmakers who like character-first genre work and who can turn a specific city and a specific family into a commercial engine.

buyer_appeal.lane: Streaming thriller / premium genre drama with international appeal
buyer_appeal.detail: The contained contemporary footprint and screen-based hacking sequences make it possible to package around a strong director and a few standout roles rather than a large star ensemble. The Nairobi setting, cybercrime angle, and family-conspiracy hook give it export value in a lane that buyers already understand and can market with a clear hook.

considerations.area: The reveal stack is doing a lot of lifting.
considerations.detail: The script keeps adding new identity turns — Jackie, the Regency, Berk, Tony, the parents, the sister, the bank file — and a next pass could consider where one or two of those reveals can arrive earlier or be braided together so the back half feels even more inevitable. The core engine is strong; the opportunity is to let the audience discover one fewer thing at a time so each turn lands harder.

considerations.area: The hacking dialogue can be dramatized more.
considerations.detail: Several scenes lean on step-by-step technical explanation — especially the early phone fix, the Juicebox operation, and the bank intrusion — and the material would pop even more if a few of those beats were expressed through decisions, interruptions, or visible consequences instead of procedure alone. The tech is already cinematic; the next pass is about letting the pressure show up in behavior as much as in code.

considerations.area: The final act is built for a contained action footprint.
considerations.detail: The warehouse showdown, car ambush, and explosion give the movie a clear climax, but they also concentrate most of the physical action into a short stretch. One lever would be to keep the same escalation while folding one of the action beats into an existing location, which would protect the pace and keep the production footprint efficient.

considerations.area: The supporting women can carry more story weight.
considerations.detail: Rose, Sophie, Monica, and Jackie each bring a distinct energy, and the script already hints at a larger female network around Mark’s life. A next pass could foreground one or two of those relationships a little earlier so the emotional architecture around Mark feels even richer before the conspiracy fully takes over.

considerations.area: The content lane is firmly mature.
considerations.detail: The torture, execution-style violence, and sexual assault testimony place this squarely in an adult thriller lane, which is a clean fit for streaming or premium buyers but not for broad family-facing platforms. That clarity helps positioning, and it also means marketing can lean into the darker, more adult side of the premise without hedging.
